APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF JULY 21, 2020

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO TIME,
SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED EXCLUSIVELY
OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:05 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Jerry Velasco, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Councilmember Velasco  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt to
  address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the
  Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will take a
  short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the
  event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session
  items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the
  meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public
  wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the Council shall
  allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into Closed
  Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized Closed
  Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a speaker’s time limit of 3
  minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall be under no obligation to
  respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or comments posed by a speaker or
  take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond such action as the City Council may
  be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized Closed Session matter pursuant to the
  Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 4.1 through 4.7.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
  6:08 pm. Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:09 pm.

  City Attorney Rick Olivarez reported out of Closed Session with respect to Items 4.1
  through 4.7.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries on
  matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their name
  and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to address
  the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be limited to
  three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their speaking time to
  other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.), the
  Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted agenda
  but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent meeting.
  The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration at a future
  meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any member
  of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor and/or Chair.
  Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions posed by speakers
  but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or questions posed. The
  Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or deliberation with any
  speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the Police
  Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-Arms of
  any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions given
  by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the meeting.
  While members of the public are free to level criticism of City policies and the action(s) or
  proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members of the public may not engage in
  behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the proceedings, including, but not
  limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the public from being heard when it is
  their opportunity to speak or which prevents members of the audience from hearing or
  seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not threaten any person with physical
  harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be interpreted as an imminent threat of
  physical harm. All persons attending the meeting must adhere to the City’s policy barring
  harassment based upon a person’s race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry,
  physical handicap, medical condition, marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – As the late iconic representative John Lewis stated when
  you see something that is not right, not fair, not just you have to speak up you have to do
  something rest in power Congressman. Thank you for being an inspiration and more so the
  epitome of fearless leadership. Community and Council it is a mockery of good
  governance when an elected member of the City Council has to resort to have their
  statement read during the public comment section of the meeting. It is a blatant disrespect
  to the 116,000 residents that live in this City to have one person the person presiding over
  the meeting in this case the Mayor censor those who are elected to represent them as well
  as those trying to participate in public meetings. Yes, I said it censored. Censorship is
  happening and you may be complicit. For clarity the definition of censor is an official who
  examines material that is about to be released such as books, news and art and
  suppresses any parts that are considered obscene, politically unacceptable or threat to
  security. I emphasize suppress any parts that are politically unacceptable. As witnessed at
  the last meeting the Mayor attempted to dismiss the public comment in effect censoring

  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of July 21, 2020

  residents he has also taken to censoring the City Council comments and communications.
  As of today the presider of our meetings has manipulated the meeting five times to not
  allow all members of this Council to discuss their Council communication items five times.
  Residents tune in to hear their ideas be voiced by the Council and they have been violated.
  This is a complete disregard for their time and their concerns. Members of the Council I ask
  a simple question when was the last time you were silenced or your first amendment rights
  stifled? The answer two weeks ago on July 7, 2020 when you were not able to openly
  discuss your items important enough to you to include on the City public agenda. Mr.
  Velasco don’t you think the community deserved to know how the census is going?
  Because I did address the Council and the community and nonetheless there were items
  issued on the last public agenda that Mr. Velasco pointed out which was the census that I
  think you would of liked to talk about at the last meeting or Mayor Pro Tem listing that she
  wanted to talk about the upcoming Farmer’s Market that had not yet started. This
  community deserves better even when you don’t have an item listed on your Council
  communications regardless if a member puts an item up for discussion on their agenda
  they should be heard. Am I fighting today to be heard the answer is absolutely. After
  experiencing censorship of the Mayor I must speak out. Am I fighting for you to be heard
  absolutely I would hate for you to have the exact same treatment. Together we can correct
  these wrongs for the good of those who have elected you to support the first amendment
  and in reverence to your responsibility to your constituents please vote to ensure that all
  members have the opportunity at each meeting to present their concerns on behalf of the
  community including public comment.

m) Councilmember Martinez Muela

  Jean Escalera – Yes, I would like to hold a Prayer El Monte Day in an area big enough to
  hold many people to Pray Together for an end of the Covid 19 virus and the end of Racism
  here in El Monte. I know there is the issue of social distancing, but if we were to section off
  an area of Lambert Park where people could gather together in Prayer it would be so nice!
  They did this recently in San Diego and I for one feel this is so needed. Last year I subbed
  as a Teacher for the elementary schools in El Monte, and was privy to some disrespectful
  students. Also, I am originally not from El Monte, and I have heard some racist comments
  from all sides. I am white, and have been told things like: "I wouldn't move to that state
  because there are too many white people, or I will not go to "that Church-Nativity Catholic
  Church because there are too many white people." I mean there is a lot of racism here and
  frankly I am tired of it. I think if people want to see a change they must stop looking at color
  etc. and look at who the person is on the inside. I think if we kept it light and just said that
  we are gathered in Prayer to put a stop to hatred and the end of the virus. It could happen if
  we tried. I think the gathering in San Diego was called Pray San Diego, and someone did a
  video of the event and it was beautiful-showing people of all races gathered together in
  prayer practicing social distancing. I know there is probably racism on all sides. I am just
  expressing my own experiences. It hurts too, because my Grandparents came from
  different countries and Great Grandparents. They were all poor trying to earn a living like
  everyone else.

  Cosme Jimenez – Good evening City Council and City Staff. Mr. Mayor I have been
  reviewing the requirements to participate during Public Comments and one of them is
  Enforcement of Decorum and the second one is Disruptive to the Orderly Conduct. My
  main concern is that you Mayor are expecting everybody to respect the Rules but looks like
  they do not apply to you when it comes to Council members that do not agree with you or
  say yes all the time. I think it is time for you to Act like a Mature Person and believe in a
  Democratic Process. Council woman Martinez and Council woman Ancona do not
  have to say yes all the time because they are representing the People of El Monte and
  have the right to Agree or Disagree. Councilwoman Morales and Councilmember
  Velasco have to say yes all the time because you help them with a lot of Money during their
  last Election. That proves that they rather Support you and follow your orders, than believe
  in a Democracy. And do not forget Mr. Mayor that people Elected 5 Council Members
  and not 3 that say yes all the time. One Last thing is related to Budget Committee that you
  want to select and you keep saying that you believe in Transparency but at the same time
  you are calling your Compadres and Comadres only and of course, they say yes all the
  time so they are qualified.

  4
   City Council Meeting Minutes of July 21, 2020

  Gabriel Ramirez – Good evening City Council, City Staff, and residents. At the previous
  City Council meeting Councilwoman Martinez-Muela and Councilwoman Ancona attempted
  to have their voices silenced by Mayor Quintero over basic protocol. Residents (mainly
  registered voters) witnessed this, as the video portion went viral on various social media
  platforms. I would like the Mayor to appreciate that this community is not naive or ignorant
  as he may believe. We may not all be lawyers, but the one thing Residents of this
  community will not stand for, is the mistreatment of our female elected officials over ego &
  macho pride. If the current Mayor for the “friendly” City of El Monte is no longer capable to
  withstand constructive criticism; maybe elected office isn’t for him anymore and he should
  consider not running for reelection. The vast majority of this community will support Mayor
  Andre Quintero to not run for reelection. Lastly, I recommend City council members seek a
  remedy to reinstate the rotating Mayor spot and not wait until next election.

  Melissa Michelson – As an elected member of the LA County Democratic Party for this
  Assembly District as well as a California Democratic Party delegate, I wish to express my
  extreme dismay at the Mayor Quintero’s treatment of Councilwoman Martinez-Muela at the
  last city council meeting. I fully appreciated her attempt to stand up for the rights of the
  public to voice their messages. I find it disturbing and frankly questionable that the mayor
  was supposedly "acting on the advice of counsel", as he said, to summarize the letters to
  be entered into the record rather than read them aloud. It is also unacceptable that when
  public letters in El Monte City Hall are read aloud, that any councilmember interject their
  own commentary, like the Mayor did, as seen in a July 10 posting of the video that is
  making its way all over the Internet. Councilwoman Martinez-Muela was right to correct him
  on that point, but that is when the Mayor unprofessionally raised his voice at her saying that
  HE was the one that had the mic and then he continued commenting on the public’s letter
  that there was no truth in it, completely ignoring what the Councilwoman was trying to tell
  him before he rudely and aggressively interrupted her. This disturbing exchange and
  behavior from the mayor serves as an example to other municipal governments as to how
  NOT to conduct a city council meeting, and I expect that Mr. Quintero first and foremost
  publically apologize to the councilwoman, and immediately cease such conduct in the
  future.

  Antonio Perez – Hello El Monte City Council, As a concerned citizen of El Monte I'm very
  concerned why are we having Farmers Market during the pandemic COVID-19? I'm sure
  you are well aware according to Los Angeles County Department of Public Health El Monte
  COVID 19 cases 2,578, and 76 death cases, it is very contradicting to Mayor Andre
  Quintero and those who agree to put on the Farmers Market during this difficult times. You
  are putting El Monte residents and other community members from outside of El Monte at
  risk. I recommend city council to effective immediately cancel Famers Market until we are
  cleared. Do the right thing for the sake of the community please have the compassion and
  protect the lives of the community not putting them on jeopardy.

  Charles Hoffman – My name is Chuck Hoffman, resistant of The City of El Monte. Good
  evening, Council members, city staff and public. It saddens me one cannot attend council
  meetings at this time, to voice their concerns of what is going on in our city to this council in
  person! I have been very disappointed with the council meetings as of late for many
  reasons! (Yes I am watching) Some of your members have been going after elected
  officials and city staff, because they do not seem to jump high enough and they seem
  unable to understand why they don’t jump as high as they want them too! Why one thinks
  the city is not being transparent just because they seem to have blinders on and do not
  know or ask or wish to listen or read what is going on? Council Communication: (City
  Council is unable to address or complete all agenized Closed Session items by 7:00 p.m.,
  the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the meeting, immediately
  following Council Communications) So it is written and if the meetings were to start at 7pm
  there might be time to get to some council communication and maybe not? Also it would
  not hurt to have council limited to a time for their communication, has the public is for their
  public comments! I wish to leave you with these thoughts. This is our City not your City but
  our City! No one asking me what I think! Before this pandemic I had a cow that die. (MY
  COW IS DEAD; I DO NOT NEED YOUR BULL.) I trust I’ve addressed this council as a
  whole? Thank you for this time to express couple of my thoughts and concerns, there are a
  lot much!
